newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia 1997 wheat crop seen up 8-9 pct.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia 1997 wheat crop seen up 8-9 pct.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIAN 97 WHEAT OUTPUT SEEN RISING TO 36.5-39.5 MILLION TONNES
MOSCOW, July 14 - Russia's total wheat production is now forecast in the range of 36.5-39.5 million tonnes, a rise of eight to nine percent on last year.
The higher outlook is due to an increase in the spring wheat area combined with good development of winter wheat plantings.

However, production forecasts at this stage remain quite tentative, particularly for the Urals and Siberia. The final outcome will depend crucially on weather conditions until the beginning of large-scale harvesting in September.
By mid-June, Russia had completed its spring wheat sowing campaign.
A decline in winter wheat plantings was offset by an increase in the spring wheat area.
As a result, the total wheat area for 1997 remains nearly identical to last year's record level of 25.7 million hectares (Table 1).
Most major wheat-producing areas increased acreages, particularly in the European part of Russia.
In Siberia, plantings declined against the previous year but were still above the average seen in recent years.

Though some wheat areas (the extreme southern parts of Western Siberia, the eastern part of the North Caucasus) have suffered hot and dry weather, weather conditions in May-June were favourable for wheat development in most regions, particularly for winter wheat in the Central Chernozem (Black Earth) region and in the North Caucasus.
As a result, yields are forecast to increase in most areas.
While yield forecasts for Western and Eastern Siberia remain quite tentative, early sowing in Siberia may result in higher yields due to reduced losses during harvesting.
